findings.description: ClickzettaConnectionPool configures cz.sql.string.literal.escape.mode='quote', which leaves backslashes literal. This Python string emits SQL ESCAPE '\\', a two-character escape literal, instead of the single backslash used by escape_like_pattern. Every fallback LIKE query can then fail SQL validation. Emit the one-character literal appropriate for quote mode.

findings.title: Emit a single escape character for ClickZetta quote mode

findings.description: With IRIS_TEXT_INDEX disabled, escape_like_pattern prefixes '%' and '_' with backslashes, but this query declares '|' as the escape character. Searching for '50%' or 'test_data' therefore looks for an extra literal backslash and still treats the special character as a wildcard; ordinary matching documents are omitted. Declare backslash as the SQL escape character to match the helper.
findings.failureMode: IRIS fallback search for a literal percent or underscore fails to return documents containing the query because the SQL ESCAPE character differs from the generated pattern.
findings.title: Use the helper's escape character in IRIS LIKE queries

findings.description: The 'not contains' branch now backslash-escapes its value but, unlike the other three branches, does not supply escape='\\'. findings.description: Nest emits this as `require("@calcom/features/ee/teams/services/teamService")`, but that workspace contains only `teamService.ts` and has no build script producing the corresponding JS module. The Docker/`start:prod` path runs plain Node 20, so importing this eagerly wired controller fails with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and prevents the API from starting. It also fails `noRestrictedImports`. Import `TeamService` from the existing `@calcom/platform-libraries` export instead.

findings.title: Import the built TeamService platform export

findings.description: A user whose team membership role is `MEMBER` passes `RolesGuard` with this minimum role and reaches `TeamService.createInvite`, which performs no authorization check. They receive a usable invite URL and can invite outsiders without admin authority. The existing invite handler requires OWNER/ADMIN, and the new non-admin E2E test expects 403. Change this decorator to `TEAM_ADMIN`.
findings.failureMode: An authenticated non-admin team member can generate usable team invitation links and invite outsiders without admin authority.
findings.title: Restrict invite creation to team admins

findings.description: For a sub-team of a non-platform organization with Admin API access disabled, a valid team admin can obtain an invite through this new generic route even though the equivalent organization invite endpoint rejects them via `IsAdminAPIEnabledGuard`. Neither `RolesGuard` nor `TeamService.createInvite` checks that entitlement. Resolve the parent organization and enforce its Admin API access check before creating the invite.
findings.failureMode: The newly exposed generic team invitation route bypasses the existing organization Admin API entitlement/access restriction.
findings.title: Retain organization Admin API access checks

findings.description: Fresh invites return the constant `invite-link-for-teamId-<id>` identifier instead of the random value saved in `verificationToken.token`. Repeated requests therefore return identical `data.token` values, the URL contains a different token, and redeeming the returned value gives `Invite not found`. Return `newToken.token`, consistent with the reuse branch.
findings.failureMode: Fresh invites return a constant, non-redeemable token instead of the token saved to the database; token-only clients fail and the new token/link and uniqueness assertions fail.
findings.title: Return the verification token, not its identifier

findings.description: For a standalone team (`parentId: null`, `isOrganization: false`), this inverted condition now generates a `/signup` link. Signup's `getServerSideProps` redirects an already signed-in invitee to `/` before processing the token, so they never receive the team invitation. Org/sub-team links are also reversed to `/teams`, skipping their signup/onboarding flow. Restore `!isOrgContext`.
findings.failureMode: A signed-in user following a regular team's generated invite is redirected to the homepage without creating or showing their team membership; org/sub-team links also skip signup/onboarding.
findings.title: Restore context-specific invite destinations

Remove the blanket iPad exclusion so tests that change the theme still restore it.

findings.title: Restore the light theme after iPad dark-mode tests

findings.description: write_and_make_executable now returns FileWriteError, while prepare_tools returns crate::Result and uses ? at all five call sites. crate::Error has no From<FileWriteError> implementation, so Linux builds fail with E0277; implementing std::error::Error does not provide that conversion. Convert FileWriteError into crate::Error before propagating it.

findings.title: Provide the custom error conversion

For proactive mode put the selected status in after and the other statuses in expect in both components.

findings.description: Clearing Expected Events splits the empty string into [""], so lines.length is always positive and the form stores expect=[""]. EventTriggerSchema accepts it, but the backend compares that pattern literally, so no real event is expected and the reactive trigger never fires; an empty array would match any event. Handle an empty textarea explicitly as [] rather than storing an empty-string pattern.
findings.failureMode: Clearing the custom expected-events textarea stores an empty-string pattern that matches no real events instead of an empty-set wildcard.
findings.title: Normalize an empty expected-events textarea
